Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for a productive call today 
���� great to see the technical folks aligned. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the API auth / key management area we discussed: 

Summary from today's call:
- You will integrate Redwood for LLM inference on several internal services (session scoring + routing for fraud models).
- Primary integration will be server-to-server (backend calls), with occasional client-side reads for embeddings (read-only).
- Requirements: short-lived credentials preferred, auditable access, rotation every 90 days, and ability to use service accounts per environment (prod/staging).

Questions / clarifications we captured:
1) Do you require OAuth2 flows for user-level calls, or will initial integration be purely machine-to-machine (service accounts)?
2) Are there existing KMS/HSM integrations you need us to use for custody of keys?
3) Expected request volume for inference (tokens/sec) so we can recommend batching/connection pool settings.

Proposed next steps:
- Rishi (cc'd) will propose two approaches by EOD tomorrow: (A) API keys with automated rotation via our service-account broker, and (B) OAuth2/JWT with short-lived tokens issued by FintechCo's identity provider.
- Monica will attach the integration checklist and a short sample for service-account based auth (node/python snippets).
- Alex / Priya: please send us your KMS provider and a rough traffic estimate so we can finalize recommendations.

Attachments: integration checklist (spreadsheet) and a short one-pager on our service-account + rotation flow included in follow-up.

If that looks right, we'll sync on implementation owners and timeline.

Best,

����--- attaching the items we discussed. Highlights included and next steps below.

Attachments included:
- fintechco-integration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet with required fields and stub examples)
- redwood-service-account-guidance.pdf (how our service-account broker works, rotation cadence, and example policies)
- SOC2-extract.pdf (requested SOC2 extract, redacted)

High-level recommendation (for MVP):
1) Start with service-account based integration. We will:
   - Create a Redwood managed service account per FintechCo environment (staging/prod).
   - Use short-lived tokens minted by Redwood's broker; tokens expire in 1 hour.
   - Store long-term key material in your AWS KMS; Redwood will integrate via IAM role with restricted decrypt/sign permissions.
2) Rotation & audit:
   - Automated rotation: Redwood rotates underlying signing keys every 90 days; short-lived tokens mean no client-side rotation required.
   - Audit logs: we will provide per-token issuance logs (timestamp, service-account, scope, request-id) and per-request logs for inference calls.
3) OAuth2/JWT option (Phase 2):
   - If you need user-level delegation later, we can support OIDC flows and accept tokens from your IdP; we'll map scopes to model/route permissions.

Next steps / asks for FintechCo:
- Confirm AWS account/role we can use for KMS access and the name of the KMS key (or we can accept signed tokens from your side).
- Share expected ramp (we have the 150 RPS target noted) and desired pilot start date.

Internal owners: Rishi (architecture docs) / Monica (snippets & checklist) / Marissa (pilot coordination + SOC2 docs).

If helpful, we can set a 30-min technical kickoff this week to get a sandbox up.

Best,

Marissa Cole
